summary.name: SaneHosts
summary.one_liner: A macOS app that manages the system hosts file to block ads, trackers, and malware domains across all apps, using curated blocklists and five protection levels.
keywords: block ads in all apps mac
use_cases: Blocking ads and trackers in every Mac app, not just browsers
Reducing telemetry and data collection from system apps
Blocking adult and gambling sites for family use
Limiting social media distractions during focus work
Switching between blocking profiles for work or family
summary.what_it_does: SaneHosts edits the Mac's built-in hosts file so domains on chosen blocklists resolve to nowhere, which affects Safari, Chrome, Slack, games and other apps. It ships 200+ curated blocklists from sources such as Steven Black, Hagezi and AdGuard, grouped into five protection levels from about 170K to 700K entries. Users can create unlimited profiles, import blocklists from files or URLs, merge profiles, and switch profiles from the menu bar. macOS asks for Touch ID or password before each hosts change, automatic backups allow rollback, and the DNS cache is flushed on activation. The page states it blocks by domain only and cannot hide empty ad boxes or ads served from the same domain as content.
notable: Manages the built-in macOS hosts file, with no VPN or proxy
Five one-click protection levels plus custom profiles
Requires Touch ID or password for hosts changes, with automatic backups
Listed in StevenBlack/hosts repository and in awesome-mac lists
caveats: Paid after a 14-day free trial: $14.99 one-time, or $49.99 for the Everything Bundle
Domain-based blocking cannot hide empty ad boxes or ads served from the same domain as content
